pass_a_gloss: And let us call to mind also the things in which we have sinned, and that it is not possible to take forgiveness of sins apart from baptism, and that it is not possible according to the gospel laws to be baptized again with water and spirit for forgiveness of sins, and that a baptism is given to us, the one of martyrdom. For thus it has been named, as is plain from the fact that to 'are you able to drink the cup which I drink' is added 'or to be baptized with the baptism which I am baptized'; and in another place it has been said: 'and I have a baptism to be baptized, and how I am held tight until it be finished'. And attend whether the baptism according to martyrdom, as the one of the Saviour has become purifying for the cosmos, it too comes to be for the healing of many being purified. For as those sitting beside the altar according to the law of Moses seemed to serve through blood of goats and bulls forgiveness of sins to those people, so the souls of those cut down with the axe on account of the witness of Jesus, not sitting beside the altar in the heavens to no purpose, serve forgiveness of sins to those praying. And at the same time we know also that, as the chief priest Jesus the Christ brought himself forward as sacrifice, so the priests, of whom he is chief priest, bring themselves forward as sacrifice; on account of which they are seen at the altar as at a place of their own. But of the priests, those faultless and bringing forward faultless sacrifices were tending the divine, while those blamed with faults, which Moses wrote up in Leviticus, were being banished from the altar. And who is the faultless priest bringing forward a faultless offering except the one holding on to the confession and fulfilling every number which the account of martyrdom demands back? About which we have said before in the things above.
pass_b_english: Let us also remember the sins we have committed, and that it is not possible to receive forgiveness of sins without baptism, and that under the laws of the Gospel it is not possible to be baptized a second time with water and the Spirit for the forgiveness of sins, and that the baptism of martyrdom is given to us. For that is what it is called, as is plain from the fact that “Can you drink the cup that I drink?” is followed by “or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?” (Mark 10:38); and elsewhere it is said, “I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how hard pressed I am until it is accomplished!” (Luke 12:50).

And consider whether the baptism of martyrdom, just as the Saviour's became a cleansing for the world, itself also serves for the healing of many who are being cleansed. For as those who attended the altar under the law of Moses were thought to minister forgiveness of sins to the people of that time through the blood of goats and bulls (Hebrews 9:13), so the souls of “those beheaded for the testimony of Jesus” (Revelation 20:4), who do not attend the altar in heaven in vain, minister forgiveness of sins to those who pray.

At the same time we also know that, just as the high priest Jesus Christ offered himself as a sacrifice, so the priests whose high priest he is offer themselves as a sacrifice; and because of that sacrifice they are seen beside the altar as in their own proper place. But among the priests, those who were without blemish and offered sacrifices without blemish served the Deity, while those marked with the blemishes that Moses recorded in Leviticus (Leviticus 21:17-21) were banished from the altar. And who is the priest without blemish, offering a victim without blemish, if not the one who holds fast to his confession and fulfils every number that the account of martyrdom requires? We have spoken of this earlier.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 30); the old English turned Origen's statements into questions ('Is forgiveness of sins to be had without baptism? And when ... to be baptized again ...?'), reversing his plain statements that forgiveness is not possible without baptism and that a second baptism in water is not possible; and it dropped the rest of the chapter (the baptism of martyrdom as cleansing for many, the souls at the heavenly altar, the martyrs as priests offering themselves, the blemished priests). Here every clause is restored and his statements stay statements.
Read καὶ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστι δυνατόν: a statement ('and that it is not possible'), parallel to the preceding καὶ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν.
Koetschau prints πῶς (with M and Luke 12:50); rendered as an exclamation.
